title: E. Array Equalizer
statement:
Jeevan has two arrays a and b of size n. He is fond of performing weird operations on arrays. This time, he comes up with two types of operations:

He wants to convert array a into an array b using the minimum total number of operations. However, Jeevan seems to have forgotten the value of b_1. So he makes some guesses. He will ask you q questions corresponding to his q guesses, the i-th of which is of the form:

Help him by answering each question.

The first line contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·10^5) — the size of arrays a and b.

The second line contains n integers a_1, a_2, ..., a_n (1 ≤ a_i ≤ 10^6).

The third line contains n integers b_1, b_2, ..., b_n (1 ≤ b_i ≤ 10^6 for i ≠ 1; b_1 = -1, representing that the value of b_1 is unknown).

The fourth line contains a single integer q (1 ≤ q ≤ 2·10^5) — the number of questions.

Each of the following q lines contains a single integer x_i (1 ≤ x_i ≤ 10^6) — representing the i-th question.

Output q integers — the answers to each of his q questions.

Consider the first test case.

[3, 7] xrightarrow[decrease]i = 1 [2, 6] xrightarrow[decrease]i = 1 [1, 5]

Hence the answer is 2.

[3, 7] xrightarrow[decrease]i = 2 [3, 6] xrightarrow[decrease]i = 2 [3, 5] xrightarrow[increase]i = 1 [4, 6] xrightarrow[decrease]i = 2 [4, 5]

Hence the answer is 4.

[3, 7] xrightarrow[decrease]i = 2 [3, 6] xrightarrow[decrease]i = 2 [3, 5]

Hence the answer is 2.

Input:
```
2
3 7
-1 5
3
1
4
3
```

Output:
```
2
4
2
```

Input:
```
6
2 5 4 1 3 6
-1 4 6 2 3 5
3
1
8
4
```

Output:
```
10
29
9
```
